messages:
sam: Quick heads-up — PR #9120 (request-routing-refactor) is blocked on an RFC link / architecture sign-off. I updated the PR description but didn't attach the formal RFC yet. Can someone on arch take a quick look?

katie: I'm available this morning, pinged @arch-committee. Do we need a short SLO/rollback appendix to land?

mike: I sketched an RFC draft here: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/req-routing-refactor — still rough but covers shard affinity + fallback routing.

sam: Thanks Mike. Yes, we need a short SLO delta paragraph and a one-line rollback plan in the RFC or PR to make the gate checks happy.

katie: I'll add an "SLO impact" section and an explicit canary plan in the PR description.

arch-bot: Note: Changes that touch request routing require architecture review before merge (rule: ARCH-GATE-3).

mike: tagging @simon since this touches shard leader selection — low-risk but surface area in routing table.

simon: Will review this afternoon. Quick question: will this change affect canary behavior for dedicated pools?

sam: Short answer: yes, we'll run a 5% traffic canary for 24h with automatic rollback on latency/error thresholds. Example canary command in ops runbook: `canary run --route request-routing --percent 5 --duration 24h --rollback-on error_rate>0.5% latency_p95>200ms`.

simon: OK — if you add the SLO appendix + that canary snippet in the PR or RFC, I can approve.

katie: Adding both now — will update the PR and ping when done.

sam: Appreciate it. Marking merge blocked until arch signoff.

katie: Update complete: PR description and RFC now include SLO delta and the canary + rollback plan (links in the PR). Pinged @simon.

simon: Reviewed — LGTM from me. No concerns on shard correctness.

arch-committee: Endorsement from arch-committee: no objections, recommend standard canary window. :thumbsup:

sam: Great — plan to merge tomorrow 03:00 UTC during low traffic window, will monitor dashboards and keep rollback ready. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround.
